title: A linked-list node
note: A pointer, two ints, and a byte. The recovered layout matches the source, and the trailing bytes after the char are padding the compiler adds so the next node in an array stays 8-byte aligned.

title: A header with alignment holes
note: The fields are declared small-to-large, so the compiler inserts padding to keep each one aligned: three bytes after the char, and six after the short before the 8-byte id. The access pattern reveals the holes — recovering them is how you get a struct layout right.

title: Mixed field sizes, two holes
note: Declared short, long, int, char — a jumble of sizes. The compiler pads the short up to the long's 8-byte alignment and pads the tail, so the 15 bytes of fields occupy 24. Two holes fall out of the access pattern.

title: Four ints, packed tight
note: Four equal-sized fields in a row need no padding at all — the recovered layout is a solid 16 bytes with no holes. Ordering fields large-to-small (or equal) is how you avoid the padding the other structs show.
